name: Dark Bluish Grey-Green
lede: Dark Bluish Grey-Green is a dark bluish shade of [[grey-green|grey-green]], one of Robert Ridgway's working names built by the plain grammar of modifier plus base color.

sections.title: A modifier, not a new color
sections.body: Dark Bluish Grey-Green stacks three modifiers in sequence, *dark* and *bluish*, onto the compound base color [[grey-green]] [1][4]. The nearest named colors on file are [[michigan]], [[invisible-green]] and [[dusky-bluish-green]], at 3, 4.1 and 5.4 ΔE [1][4]. The ISCC-NBS system calls this darker block, 150, 'grayish green,' a Delta-E of 8.1 from Ridgway's point [2]. A still-darker sibling, [[deep-bluish-grey-green]], extends the same grammar one tone further [1][4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this shade, as photographed, in 0.83% of 23,781 paintings, 197 paintings; within a single canvas it reads as a distinct area in 83 of them [3]. That ranks it more common than 56% of the archive's named colors [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, found in 1.2% of that century's 1,674 paintings, 3.4 times the expected rate[3]. Inside a painting it most often plays a hidden color, by lightness rank, in 55% of its 83 appearances [3]. Gustav Klimt is its most devoted painter, using it in 4 of his 50 works here, 6.3 times the baseline rate of the museums those paintings come from [3]. The earliest dated appearance is a painting from the year 1000[3]. That is 912 years before the name's first documented record in 1912, but the archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor and not a first [3].

origin.named_after: the base color grey-green, with the modifier 'dark bluish'
